outcome.description: After a ten-day bench trial the court held the unsigned subcontracts governed, found the subcontractor entitled to $71,897.70 on the three buildings ($10,065 office, $28,011.30 molding, $33,821.40 pulping), denied recovery on the payment bonds, and on the counterclaim awarded the project owner $42,414 for the reasonable value of the stairs, offset under the cross-default provisions, leaving the subcontractor a net $29,483.70 ($36,304.51 with interest). The merits judgment was affirmed per curiam (357 So. 3d 116, Fla. 4th DCA 2023). A successor judge then awarded the subcontractor $446,628.65 in prevailing-party attorney's fees and costs; on May 15, 2024 the Fourth District reversed that award in its entirety and remanded for an award of attorney's fees to the defendants (under the $62,000 joint proposal for settlement and the bond-claim fee statute).
outcome.attorneysFeesOnAppeal: reversed; fees directed to the defendants instead (amount to be set on remand)
outcome.finalNote: Merits judgment affirmed per curiam in 2023; the subcontractor's $446,628.65 fee-and-cost award was reversed in 2024 and fees were directed to the defendants, so the subcontractor's net position after fees is well below the $29,483.70 damages figure.
